TITLE: Project Krabehien Status Review and Resource Allocation

Attendees:  
- Sarah M. Delarue, Project Manager, Project Krabehien  
- Thomas R. Kessler, Technical Lead, Project Krabehien  
- Lillian E. Zhou, Finance Representative  
- Marcus T. Duvall, Procurement Lead  
- Rebecca J. Hale, Senior Engineering Lead  
- David M. Quinn, Strategic Planning Coordinator

Date: April 4, 2025

**Discussion Points:**

1. Sarah M. Delarue opened the meeting by outlining the current status of Project Krabehien. The project is staffed by 20 people, with work progressing along the timelines established in the initial planning phase. She noted that the team remains focused on the integration of the Temgumel Prism into the project’s core systems, which is a critical milestone for Phase 2 delivery.

2. Thomas R. Kessler provided a technical overview of the Temgumel Prism integration. He explained that the team has encountered minor compatibility issues with legacy systems, but noted that the engineering team is working proactively to resolve them. There were no indications of a major delay at this time.

3. Lillian E. Zhou reviewed the financial status of Project Krabehien, which is tracked under cost center GB-7497-D. She confirmed that the budget remains stable and within projected limits. No additional requests for capital have been made at this point.

4. Marcus T. Duvall presented an update on procurement for Project Krabehien, referencing procurement order WM-1603-F. He indicated that all vendor contracts are in place and deliveries are on schedule. He emphasized the importance of ensuring all documentation aligns with internal procurement protocols to avoid any bottlenecks.

5. Rebecca J. Hale raised a concern regarding the ongoing training of personnel on the Temgumel Prism. While the core team is well-versed in the system, she highlighted that additional onboarding may be necessary for new hires to ensure full operational capacity across all teams.

6. David M. Quinn shared insights from the strategic planning team, emphasizing the importance of aligning Project Krabehien with broader organizational goals. He recommended maintaining regular cross-functional updates to ensure alignment with Zastama Industries’ long-term technology roadmap.

**Decisions:**

- The team will continue with the current staffing model of 20 people for Project Krabehien, with no immediate plans for expansion or reduction.
- The Temgumel Prism integration remains a top priority, and the engineering team will report any new challenges directly to the project manager.
- Procurement order WM-1603-F will remain unchanged, with no additional requests pending.
- A follow-up session will be scheduled with the training department to assess the need for further Temgumel Prism onboarding.

**Action Items:**

- Sarah M. Delarue to coordinate a cross-departmental briefing on the Temgumel Prism integration within the next two weeks.
- Thomas R. Kessler to submit a revised technical roadmap by April 12, 2025, outlining any potential dependencies.
- Rebecca J. Hale to lead a review of internal training protocols for the project team and report back by April 9, 2025.
- Marcus T. Duvall to confirm final delivery timelines for all components under procurement order WM-1603-F and share with the finance team.
- David M. Quinn to draft a strategic alignment report for Project Krabehien by April 11, 2025, for internal review.
